comments.body: Code review found a correctness defect in the planned design and it has been remediated. The plan had TemporalStarter.start raise UnresolvableBaseBranch with _start catching it around ctx.ledger.run_once. That raise happens inside the _launch effect, after ctx.execution_seeder.seed and after the task snapshot capture. PostgresSideEffectLedger.reserve only returns replayed=True for a _COMPLETED row, and its insert uses on_conflict_do_nothing, so an effect that raises leaves the key _PENDING forever. Every later reconcile pass would re-run _launch, seeding another execution and capturing another snapshot for as long as the branch stayed unresolvable. The remediation validates the declared branch before the ledger effect runs. A new IntakeBaseResolver protocol exposes resolve_base, IntakeContext carries an optional base_resolver, and TemporalStarter implements it over the same remote_head call. Both production wiring sites pass the starter as the resolver. _start now holds the ticket before any seeding. The starter raise is retained as a guard for contexts with no resolver wired. Scope is unchanged, an undeclared ticket still uses github_default_base_branch and is never held by this path.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Every execution opens its pull request against one branch for the whole platform. `TemporalStarter.start` at `intake_runtime.py:49` sets `base = self._settings.github_default_base_branch`, which reaches the pull request unchanged via `DraftPullRequestInput.base` at `draft_pull_request.py:213` into `PullRequestInput.base` at line 742.

A per-ticket base is already modelled and already dead. `IntakeStart.base` is declared at `intake_reconciler.py:44`, its only construction site at line 365 never sets it, and the starter overwrites it regardless.

So work depending on an unmerged change cannot be automated. A ticket whose fix only makes sense atop another open pull request must target the default branch, so its diff either carries the parent change as noise or does not apply. This blocks the pilot against `archive-massgov-pfml`, where the fix for ticket `98b3-e6e7-689f-4ae0` needs the Storybook story added by pull request 14 on `joeoakhart/PFMLPB-33758` to be exercised at all.

## Approach

Let a ticket declare its base branch, and honour that declaration at intake.

The declaration travels as a `base:<branch>` label. Labels are the one ticket attribute both sources already normalise to a common shape, so one parser serves both backends and a client on either declares a stacked base the same way. That beats a rebar-only field or a setting, and a setting is wrong regardless of backend because the base varies per ticket while a setting is per deployment.

Parsing happens in `route_candidate`, not the adapters. Both sources funnel through it, from `intake_reconciler.py:238` and `rebar_intake.py:64`, and it is where `_hold` lives. Parsing in an adapter would fail during candidate construction, outside any handler, so one malformed ticket would abort the pass.

The declaration is an override, so `github_default_base_branch` stays authoritative for any ticket declaring nothing. Repeating one value is a duplicate and resolves to it. Two different values is a conflict with no defensible winner, so the ticket is held rather than settled by list order. A conflict is returned as data, not raised. `declared_base` yields a `BaseDeclaration` carrying either a branch or a conflict reason.

The failure mode is closed. An empty `base_sha` is not inert. It is the workspace checkout commit at `draft_pull_request.py:426` and the fallback gate commit at line 618, so a mistyped branch would root an execution at no known commit. Falling back to the default would silently target the wrong branch. The one exception here is `UnresolvableBaseBranch`, raised by the starter and caught in `_start` around the ledger call, so both hold paths converge on `_hold`.

An absent branch differs from a failed lookup. `remote_head` passes `check=True`, so a transient `git ls-remote` failure keeps propagating as today. Only an empty result, a successful lookup matching no ref, holds the ticket.

## Scope

- `services/orchestration/intake_base.py` is new, holding `declared_base`, `BaseDeclaration`, and `UnresolvableBaseBranch`.
- `services/orchestration/intake_reconciler.py` parses the declaration in `route_candidate`, holds on a conflict, passes the branch through `_start` as `IntakeStart.base`, and holds when the starter reports it unresolvable. `IntakeStart.base` defaults to `""` not `"main"`, so the setting stays the only place the default is named. No adapter changes.
- `services/orchestration/intake_runtime.py` honours `start.base` when set and raises when `remote_head` returns empty.
- `README.md` documents the convention, override precedence, and hold behaviour.
- Tests: `tests/unit/test_intake_base.py` is new for parsing. `tests/unit/test_intake_runtime.py` is amended, since it already exercises `TemporalStarter.start` with `remote_head` monkeypatched and `base` defaulted at lines 40 and 76. `test_intake_reconciler.py` gains the hold paths.

## Grounded assumptions

- The workflow already supports an arbitrary base. `DraftPullRequestInput.base` at `draft_pull_request.py:213` reaches `PullRequestInput.base` at line 742 without consulting the setting, so only intake selection is missing.
- Both sources expose labels under one key. `rebar_backend.py:97` writes `"labels": list(ticket.get("tags") or [])` and `jira/normalize.py:42` writes `"labels": list(self.labels)`, so one parser covers both.
- Both sources funnel through one routing function, `route_candidate`, called at `intake_reconciler.py:238` for Jira and `rebar_intake.py:64` for rebar, so parsing there needs no per-backend branch.
- `IntakeStart.base` has no current effect. Its only construction site is `intake_reconciler.py:365` and it omits `base`, so changing the default from `"main"` to `""` cannot alter any existing execution.
- An unresolved branch yields an empty string, not an error. `remote_head` at `intake_runtime.py:25` returns `proc.stdout.split()[0] if proc.stdout.strip() else ""`, and `git ls-remote` exits 0 for an unmatched ref.
- A starter exception would otherwise abort the pass. `PostgresSideEffectLedger.run_once` at `idempotency.py:108` does not catch effect exceptions, so `_start` must catch it.
- The pilot branch exists. `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/joeoakhart/PFMLPB-33758` in `archive-massgov-pfml` returns `b0117d05d8`, the head of pull request 14.

## Testing

Happy path: a candidate carrying `base:feature-x` starts a workflow on `feature-x` at its remote head.

Failure and edge paths, each an acceptance criterion below: no label, an empty value, a prefix-only label such as `baseline`, a duplicate value, two conflicting values, a branch name containing a colon, an unresolvable branch, a second candidate still starting after a hold, and a `git ls-remote` failure propagating rather than holding. The prefix matches case-sensitively because branch names do.

Live end to end: the pilot ticket for `98b3-e6e7-689f-4ae0` opens a pull request in `archive-massgov-pfml` based on `joeoakhart/PFMLPB-33758`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A candidate carrying `base:<branch>` starts a workflow based on that branch (`tests/unit/test_intake_runtime.py`).
- [ ] Its `base_sha` is resolved from the declared branch (same module).
- [ ] A candidate with no `base:` label starts a workflow based on `github_default_base_branch` (same module).
- [ ] A declared branch that does not resolve starts no workflow (reconciler test asserting `IntakeReport.started` is empty).
- [ ] That same ticket is recorded in `IntakeReport.held` with a reason naming the branch (same test).
- [ ] Two conflicting `base:` labels start no workflow and record a hold naming both (reconciler test).
- [ ] A held ticket does not stop a second candidate in the same pass from starting (reconciler test, two candidates).
- [ ] An empty declaration such as `base:` falls back to the default branch (`tests/unit/test_intake_base.py`).
- [ ] A label such as `baseline` is not read as a declaration (same module).
- [ ] Repeating `base:x` resolves to `x` (same module).
- [ ] A declared branch containing a colon is preserved in full (same module).
- [ ] `declared_base` reports a conflict as data, raising nothing (same module).
- [ ] A `git ls-remote` failure propagates instead of holding (test raising `CalledProcessError` from `remote_head`).
- [ ] [non-codebase] A live run of the pilot ticket for `98b3-e6e7-689f-4ae0` opens a pull request against `archive-massgov-pfml` whose base branch is `joeoakhart/PFMLPB-33758`.
  provenance: environment=local-colima-k3s; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the pilot executes the shipped intake and workflow path against the client repository over the same Temporal path a deployment uses
- [ ] `README.md` names the `base:<branch>` label convention.
- [ ] `README.md` states that the setting applies when no label is present.
- [ ] `README.md` states that an unresolvable or conflicting declaration holds it.
- [ ] `ruff check services tests scripts adapters` exits 0.
